headline: Bank Negara blocked 162,642 mule accounts in 2025; investment-scam losses still rose 73%
context: Bukit Aman's Commercial Crime Investigation Department reported that non-existent-investment scams cost Malaysians RM1.47 billion across 9,603 cases in 2025, up from RM848.6 million across 6,337 in 2024, even as the state disrupted record numbers of mule accounts.

cards.big: Investment-scam losses hit RM1.47 billion in 2025, up 73% from RM848.6 million a year earlier.
cards.sub: CCID director Rusdi Mohd Isa gave the figure on 18 April 2026: 9,603 cases, against 6,337 in 2024.

cards.big: The second hit lands after the 'profit': victims see fake gains, then pay 'fees' to withdraw money that never existed.
cards.sub: CCID's funnel: lure on Facebook or Instagram, shift to WhatsApp or Telegram, show fake dashboard profits, then demand fees and taxes to release them.

cards.big: The state was not idle: Bank Negara stopped 162,642 suspected mule accounts in 2025. The losses still rose.
cards.sub: The Securities Commission added 249 entities to its investor-alert list and blocked 175 scam websites the same year. The money kept finding a route.

cards.big: It is not only more victims. The average case lost more: about RM153,000, up from RM134,000 a year earlier.
cards.sub: RM1.47 billion over 9,603 cases, against RM848.6 million over 6,337 in 2024. Cases rose about 52%; losses rose about 73%.

cards.big: Malaysia's 2026 online-safety law forces platforms to pull scam content faster. It still makes no one repay the victim.
It is a fire service that finally inspects the wiring but still owes nothing when the house burns down.
cards.sub: The wiring is the platform and the payment rail. The new code demands risk checks, not repayment.

cards.big: Warnings are cheap. The question Malaysia still ducks: who pays when the money clears every checkpoint and vanishes?

sources: Bernama 18 Apr 2026 (CCID dir Rusdi Mohd Isa); Malay Mail 18 Apr 2026; The Sun 18 Apr 2026; The Star 19 Apr 2026; Sinar Daily 18 Apr 2026; BNM Annual Report 2025; SC Annual Report 2025 Part 2 Table 17; Online Safety Act 2025; MCMC Risk Mitigation Code 2026
